items.stem: Define the term 'free goods'.
items.answer: Goods such as air that are available in plenty and have no price.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the idea: goods such as air that are available in plenty and have no price.

items.stem: Why does scarcity lead to the need to choose?
items.answer: (1) Resources are limited but wants are unlimited. (2) Using a resource for one purpose means it cannot be used for another.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: (1) Resources are limited but wants are unlimited. (2) Using a resource for one purpose means it cannot be used for another.

items.stem: Harleen, a farmer in Haryana, can use one acre of land to grow wheat (expected income ₹69,000), mustard (expected income ₹53,000) or vegetables (expected income ₹48,000). Harleen decides to grow wheat. What is the opportunity cost of this decision?
items.answer: ₹53,000 (the income from mustard, the next best alternative)
items.markingKey: Opportunity cost = value of the next best alternative given up = income from mustard = ₹53,000. The third option is not counted.

items.stem: Saanvi can earn ₹300 an hour giving tuition. On Sunday Saanvi spends 5 hours at a cricket match instead. What is the opportunity cost of watching the match?
items.answer: ₹1,500 of tuition income given up
items.markingKey: Opportunity cost = income forgone = ₹300 × 5 = ₹1,500.

What is the opportunity cost of raising tractor output from 2 to 3, and what does the pattern of the table show?
items.answer: 30 tonnes of wheat; the opportunity cost rises as more tractors are produced
items.markingKey: Wheat falls from 155 to 125 tonnes, so the cost is 30 tonnes (2 marks). Each extra tractor costs more wheat: increasing opportunity cost (1 mark).

items.stem: Gauri, a farmer in Haryana, can use one acre of land to grow wheat (expected income ₹81,000), mustard (expected income ₹72,000) or vegetables (expected income ₹60,000). Gauri decides to grow wheat. What is the opportunity cost of this decision?
items.answer: ₹72,000 (the income from mustard, the next best alternative)
items.markingKey: Opportunity cost = value of the next best alternative given up = income from mustard = ₹72,000. The third option is not counted.
